startup.name: Promptless
startup.one_liner: An AI teammate that automatically updates your customer-facing docs
startup.description: AI agent that updates customer facing documentation from feature releases, support tickets and internal Slack conversations, and works with any docs platform. Used by startups and larger companies. Team of 5 in San Francisco.

yc_acceptance.basis: The company is already in the batch that starts at the as_of date, so the acceptance step is reported only for completeness: the prior for a random applicant is about 1 percent (0.6 to 2 percent), and conditional on being accepted the forecast below is what matters. Team of 5 with enterprise customers claimed suggests real usage; ideas in developer tools get interest but the wedge is narrow.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly pass because documentation maintenance looks like a feature rather than a company: docs platforms such as Mintlify and GitBook already offer update agents, coding assistants can draft doc changes inside the repository, and the budget owner is unclear between support, developer relations and engineering. A team of five with claimed enterprise users is a good sign, but the market size question would likely dominate the interview.

ladder.why_it_fails: Window of 22.3 months (2025-01-06 to 2026-11-17). The likeliest miss is that docs automation looks like a feature: Mintlify, Swimm, GitBook and ReadMe already sell to the same docs owners and coding assistants can draft doc changes, so investors question the size of the budget. FifthTry (continuous documentation) raised a seed and still shut down, and Nimbic AI is a Spring 2025 neighbor, so a round above $1M needs proof of paid seats at larger firms.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A inside 22 months needs about $1M or more of ARR from companies that treat docs as a growth lever. Documentation budgets are small and sit under support or developer relations, sales cycles are slow, and coding assistants that update docs in the repo can substitute. Close analogs (Nimbic AI, FifthTry) stalled at seed, and Series A medians are near 30 months after batch start.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C needs a platform sized category position, and documentation maintenance is a small slice of software spend that docs vendors and coding assistants can absorb by adding an agent. The 2022 to 2024 B2B cohort has no Series C yet, and almost no companies of this size reach it inside two years of batch start, so the probability here is only a small floor value.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The most likely end is a stall or a small acquisition by a docs platform or support vendor: Inari and Unthread are acquired YC analogs at small scale and FifthTry, which sold continuous documentation, shut down after a seed. A larger outcome would require expanding from docs updates into the knowledge layer that support agents and coding assistants read, which is a different and more contested product.

killers.risk: Docs automation is absorbed as a feature by docs platforms and coding assistants
killers.evidence: Mintlify, Swimm and GitBook already sell to docs owners and describe agents that open doc update pull requests.
killers.mitigation: Stay platform agnostic and pull in support and Slack context which code tools lack.

killers.risk: Small budget and long sales cycles keep revenue too low for a round above $1M
killers.evidence: Mid market documentation platforms are priced at about $200 to $1,000 per month per a vendor guide.
killers.mitigation: Anchor on enterprise accounts where docs quality hits churn.

killers.risk: Agent quality errors in customer facing docs erode trust
killers.evidence: Vendor guides note that major changes still need human review, and wrong edits in customer facing docs can cause support load and lost trust.
killers.mitigation: Human approval flow and reliable source citations.

technical_complexity.rationale: Reading code, tickets and Slack and producing accurate edits across arbitrary docs platforms is feasible with current models; the hard part is trustworthy context retrieval, avoiding wrong edits and many integrations. A team of five can ship an MVP in three months but breadth of integrations takes longer.

takeover_risk.rationale: Docs platforms and coding assistants have distribution and the incentive to ship update agents quickly; a standalone vendor survives only through cross source context and enterprise workflow depth.

evidence.claim: Several vendors sell tools that keep docs in sync with code, showing paid demand but a crowded field

narrative.headline: A narrow docs agent with a thin budget category; seed odds track the anchor over a long 22 month window.
narrative.general_summary: Promptless is an AI agent that updates customer facing docs from releases, tickets and Slack. Over a 22.3 month window the B2B cohort anchor gives a seed probability near 0.54, and I report 0.52. Series A inside the same window is about 0.10. Documentation tooling has many entrants and a small budget, and the same wedge produced FifthTry, which died after a seed. The company has a team of five and claims enterprise users, which helps but does not rank it.

assumptions: Blind forecast made as of 2025-01-06 using only the YC batch description in the input file, with market-only web searches.
Forecast window is 22.3 months, from 2025-01-06 to 2026-11-17.

Seed means an outside financing round above about $1M that closes inside the window, not the standard YC deal of about $500K; the seed and Series A probabilities are window probabilities, not ever probabilities.

The odds do not rank this company against other companies in the batch: in the 2026 winners test, team size, claimed traction and a hot sector did not separate raisers from non raisers, so the seed number stays near the cohort anchor.
Cohort anchors come from older and 2022 to 2024 batches and are partly right censored; funding coverage in the data is incomplete (lower, known and upper ranges quoted).
